systems.country_label: Central African Internet Exchange (Central African Republic, not TCD)

note: Only exchange point named is CENIX in Central African Republic; nothing on an exchange in TCD.
Exchanges named (NAPAfrica, JINX, KIXP, IXPN, AMS-IX) are in South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria; Chad appears only as a Starlink market, no exchange point in TCD.

facts.fact: Digital Business Africa reports TCHADIX, Chad's internet exchange point run by ADETIC as an economic interest group (GIE), has been operational for a year, with internet access providers and mobile operators attending its members' general assembly opened on 20 May 2026; no member count is given.

systems.owner: GIE of members, promoted by ADETIC

note: Exchange points named only as a priority for regional fibre interconnection; none stated in service.

facts.fact: Internet Society Pulse's IXP Tracker lists 1 active exchange point in Chad, N'Djamena IX, with 9 members as of November 2026.
ISOC Pulse's IXP Tracker lists 1 exchange point in Chad with 8 of 18 networks peering.

note: IXPs in N'Djamena, Abeche, Mao, Moundou and Sahr are a plan only.

facts.fact: ISOC Pulse says Chad has one active IXP that connects a third of the country's networks, and that no content delivery network operates caches there.
Internet Society Pulse says Chad has one IXP managed by ADETIC, with at least nine networks peering there per PeeringDB, almost all visible networks in Chad.
Russell Southwood says the Ndjamena Internet Exchange (DJAMIX) has nine members, down from 11 in 2024, about half of them ISPs; local traffic is not available.
The minister stated that N'Djamena has an Internet Exchange Point.
Internet Society Pulse says Chad's reported IXP count, memberships and coverage all rose between March 2019 and March 2026, with coverage moving from 0 to 100 percent.
